title: Portfolio Analytics Need Major Improvement
text:
INDmoney’s investment tracking needs significant improvement. It does not display XIRR for investments held for less than one year, making it difficult to accurately evaluate short-term investment performance.

More importantly, there is no consolidated portfolio-level view showing metrics such as XIRR and total Gain/Loss across the entire portfolio, including both Stocks and Mutual Funds. Users should not have to analyze each investment category separately to understand their overall performance.

A comprehensive portfolio dashboard with consolidated XIRR, absolute returns, total invested amount, current value, and overall Gain/Loss would make the app far more useful for tracking investments.

title: Which SIP platform would you recommend for long-term investing: Zerodha Coin, Groww, Kuvera, ICICI Direct or another platform?
text:
@KaranAggarwal

For this you have to first understand the 2 methods of mutual funds buying and how they operate and what are benefits of them for you.

First method is demat method in which the mutual funds you buy gets credited to you demat account.This method is usually preferred if you invest in stocks and etfs and want your full portfolio to be managed and tracked in one place as mutual funds also come in demat account in this form. Also it has some advantages like modifying bank account is easier nominee modification is easier inheritance is easier.

For example to understand it just assume an hypothetical example 1. You want to withdraw your mutual funds but you have purchased them with x bank account now it is closed and you have to get your money in y bank account you just have to update your bank in your broker like zerodha , dhan and it will be considered for mutual funds as well. Example 2. The inheritance of demat mutual funds are also easier as you just have to do some work with your broker like zerodha , dhan and all the securities in demat account including mutual funds will be seemlessly transferred to the nominee demat account within 7 working days.

Example 3. You have to change nominee in your mutual funds you just have to change it in your broker and it is considered for mutual funds also.

Second method is SOA method where mutual funds do not come in your demat account and stay with the amc (asset management company) like hdfc amc motilal oswal amc parag parikh amc. Let’s understand this also with the above examples 1. Change of bank suppose you have 4 mutual funds with different fund houses (amc) and you want to change the bank in them changing it in the broker app or the app from where you purchase mutual funds like groww kuvera (i haven’t mentioned zerodha , dhan because they keep mutual fund in demat mode) so changing it in these app like groww kuvera don’t do the work you have to contact each amc separately for the change of bank and it also works like this that for example you have 2 folios in same amc you have to change bank in those 2 folios separately. Example 2. You have to change nominee it is also same as bank you have to change nominee in all amc separately and same work case for multiple folios in same amc you have to change nominee in multiple folios even if it is from same amc. Example 3. Inheritance you have to visit and follow the inheritance process for each and every fund house separately and for every folio separately even if it is of same amc.

Here are some apps according to their format of mutual funds (demat or soa).

Zerodha coin (demat)

Dhan (demat and soa both)

Groww (demat but you can opt out of it and can shift to soa)

Kuvera (only soa)

Upstox (demat)

Angel one (demat)

ICICI direct (demat and soa both)

Et money (soa)

You can choose any of the above but according to your conditions like easy inheritance smooth redemption process etc you should choose demat format.

You can choose any of the platform all are very safe zerodha and groww are top platforms and dhan is feature rich and new age platform with no amc and zero brokerage for delivery (zerodha also has that zero brokerage for delivery) I personally use dhan with demat form of mutual funds.

title: Equity NAV curve feature finally launched
text:
Equity NAV curve feature finally launched

Zerodha just launched the equity NAV curve feature. It basically treats your account value curve as a mutual fund and gives a similar curve. Mutual funds start at 10 NAV. Zerodha has chosen all its users to start at 1000 NAV. (10 or 1000 doesn’t make any difference)

For example if your account had 10L and you withdrew 5L, the usual curve would fall by half. But new curve won’t fall by half. It would lose half the units(like mutual funds) but the curve would move only by as much percent as it should move due to your trading/investment activity on the remaining 5L. So no big ups and down.

This also means that if you add and withdraw money throughout the year, earlier it was quite hard to calculate the ROI because capital fluctuated so much. But now you can just compare your NAV between two dates and that is the ROI. 

Screenshot_20241218-100213_Chrome1264×2780 95.8 KB
Go to zerodha dashboard. Click on down arrow next to ‘Equity Value Curve’ and change it to Portfolio Performance Beta and you will get the new curve. It’s live for everyone.
